hook_text: Your photo printed 10 × 25 instead of 20 × 30. Why does everyone look weird?
clip_script: The ten by fifteen centimetre photo and its twenty by thirty centimetre enlargement are similar. Ten times two is twenty, and fifteen times two is thirty: the same scale factor, two, for both sides. The stretched version, ten by twenty-five centimetres, is NOT similar. The width is multiplied by one, but the length by five thirds. Different scale factors mean the shape has changed.
visual_style: A smiling photo enlarges evenly to double size, then a second print stretches tall and the face elongates comically; scale-factor labels appear on each side.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to spot similar and congruent shapes like a detective.
